finding: max-w-[calc(100vw-1rem)] is dead: 100vw-1rem is always LARGER than the w-[min(...,100vw-2rem)] beside it and the popup is absolutely positioned, so it can never clamp. It also made TEST-5's viewport-relative width check pass vacuously (see the tests-quality finding on the \b regex).

The list cap calc(var(--available-height)-7rem) hardcodes a 112px chrome allowance against ~108px of real chrome — 4px of slack — and the panel itself lost the overflow backstop the old inline maxHeight provided. A Popover `title`, or any kit Button height change, silently pushes the panel past --available-height with nothing to scroll.
calc(var(--available-height) - 7rem) goes negative below ~112px available height; max-height clamps negative to 0, collapsing the list to zero height while header+footer still render.

100vw includes a classic vertical scrollbar while the INV-1 assertion measures documentElement.clientWidth, which excludes it; the 2rem gutter absorbs the ~15px today but the real margin is 17px, not 32px, and is undocumented.

data-testid="notification-bell-panel" has no consumer anywhere in the tree and cannot enter the typed registry (kitTestIds covers only kit/src + shell/src) — an unwired addition per CODING_GUIDELINES §15.

wrap-anywhere — the one genuinely new containment mechanism — had ZERO behavioural coverage. panelScrollWidth<=panelClientWidth cannot see row overflow (the ScrollArea axis=y viewport is overflow-x:hidden, a clipping scroll container), and the hOutside sweep only measures buttons, which are held by min-w-0+shrink-0 that both PREDATE this fix. Verified by mutation: with the class removed the panel still reports scrollWidth==clientWidth==340 while the token box measures 635.5px.

TEST-5(b)'s /\bw-\[[^\]]*vw[^\]]*\]/ matches max-w-[calc(100vw-1rem)] because \b matches between '-' and 'w'. A fixed w-[340px] alongside any max-w viewport bound passed the very check whose comment claims it would fail.

TEST-7 is the [acceptance] proof for INV-3 and claims to sweep the whole rendered subtree, but its regex covered only pl/pr/ml/mr + text-left/right — missing border-l/r, rounded-l/r, space-x-*, left-/right-, scroll-pl/pr — and el.className on an SVG is an SVGAnimatedString, silently exempting every lucide icon from the sweep.

The code comment asserts 'npm run lint:logical-direction enforces it on changed code'. It does not: the linter diffs the PARENT repo and its PATH_INCLUDE is src-app/{ui,desktop/ui}/src/, so an sdk submodule change is invisible to it. INV-3 was therefore unenforced on the only files this change edits, while the diff claimed otherwise.

TEST-6 asserts only that the class string CONTAINS 'min-w-0' and 'wrap-anywhere' — it restates the diff and cannot fail except by editing that literal. Its name claimed it proved 'a long unbroken token cannot widen its row'.

TEST-2's four panel-rect in-viewport assertions pass on origin/main (base-ui's shift/flip always kept the 288px panel on screen; it was the CONTENT that escaped), so they are a regression guard, not the INV-2 discriminator they were labelled as.

SELF-FOUND while fixing the above: the seed used the created_at DEFAULT, so the two adversarial rows were the OLDEST of 12 and fell outside the bell's items.slice(0,8). The long-token row was never rendered and the spec was green while exercising nothing of the sort. Caught by the new row-level assertion on its first run.

Neither spec exercised the EMPTY (0-notification) branch, which takes a different code path (<Empty> instead of the ScrollArea, no list testid at all). TEST-8's population control also lived in a separate test() with its own mount, so TEST-7's sweep had no control of its own.

DESIGN.md said the height bound works 'exactly as kit/dropdown.tsx does' (max-h-(--available-height)), while the implementation used min(26rem, calc(...-7rem)) — two undeclared constants. Design/implementation drift on the stated approach.

Component-test selector literals polluted the SHARED sdk testid registry with 9 ids, 7 of them per-fixture-row ids that can never exist in production (gen-testid-registry.mjs walks src/** including .test.tsx and matches data-testid inside selector STRINGS).

The bell is classified {kind:'via'} and the popover lives in the sdk submodule, so the overlay registry has no entry and gate:ui cannot render the OPEN popover — no runtime-health cell, no axe pass, no light/dark or visual baseline for the changed surface.
